content:
Ethan Park: kicking off a thread on the owner mapping config in control plane. need to lock down: versioning model, audit trail, and change review workflow. goal is: incident-bot + pager routing can resolve `incident_type/subtype -> owning_team` consistently.

Rafael Mendes: +1. biggest requirement from SRE side: (1) it’s auditable (who changed what / when), (2) rollbacks are safe + fast, (3) review is enforced (no “hot edits” in prod UI), and (4) we can answer “what mapping was active during incident X?”

Allison Grant: also: please don’t create a config that explodes metric label cardinality. we should keep values like `team_slug` allowlisted and stable.

Ethan Park: proposed shape (YAML-ish) is below. control plane stores it versioned; router + incident-bot consume it.

Ethan Park: ```yaml
schema_version: 1
mapping_version: "2025-11-02.1"
updated_by: "ethan.park"
updated_at: "2025-11-02T18:12:00Z"
entries:
  - incident_type: "capacity"
    incident_subtype: "gpu_exhaustion"
    primary_owner: "eng-infra-fleet"
    secondary_owners: ["eng-platform-routing"]
    consulted: ["eng-sre"]
    runbook_url: "https://confluence/.../region-failover"
  - incident_type: "routing"
    incident_subtype: "fallback_loop"
    primary_owner: "eng-platform-routing"
    secondary_owners: ["eng-infra-fleet"]
    consulted: ["eng-sre"]
    runbook_url: "https://confluence/.../routing-fallback"
``` 

Mina Haddad: question: are we committing to a single primary always? even when it’s clearly multi-cause? (capacity+router)

Rafael Mendes: for the program: yes, exactly one primary for paging + reporting. we can add contributing systems elsewhere (postmortem fields). incident commander picks one.

Ravi Menon: for routing subtypes: we should be careful w naming. “fallback_loop” vs “fallback_misbehavior” etc. if subtype taxonomy changes, does config need a new version? or do we alias?

Ethan Park: intent: taxonomy values are allowlisted enums from the taxonomy v1 doc. owner mapping config should reject unknown types/subtypes.

Dylan Brooks: from tooling side (incident-bot): best experience is strict dropdowns. if control plane is source-of-truth, we can fetch it and populate dropdown + owner auto-fill.

Devon Price: +1. also need “unknown” path. on-call will sometimes not know subtype. can config include `incident_subtype: "*"` fallback?

Ethan Park: I was thinking explicit `default` entry per type, e.g. subtype null means “any subtype not explicitly listed”. But we should avoid wildcard precedence bugs.

Allison Grant: wildcard rules make observability debugging painful. pls define deterministic precedence and log which entry matched.

Ethan Park: ok. precedence proposal:
1) exact (type+subtype)
2) type-only default (type, subtype = "")
3) global default (type="unknown")

Rafael Mendes: global default should be SRE? or “oncall-ic”? we need a real team.

Dylan Brooks: for incident-bot we can do: if unknown -> route to current on-call schedule for “sre-primary” but keep a warning that it must be updated within X minutes.

Kira Thompson: + runbook suggestion: type-only can point to classification decision tree / generic “how to triage routing vs capacity” page.

Mina Haddad: re change review: can we make updates only via PR flow? i.e. config lives in a repo and control plane pulls from main?

Ethan Park: option A: config in repo + PR review; control plane syncs from repo (like policy-as-code). option B: config stored in control plane, but updates only via “Change Request” endpoint that requires codeowner approvals.

Rafael Mendes: preference: A, unless it’s super slow. we already have review culture around YAML. also helps answer “who approved”.

Ravi Menon: A is nice but watch out: urgent fixes during incident (wrong owner) need to be fast.

Ethan Park: for urgent: can have expedited path but still audited. e.g. PR + 1 approver + “emergency” label, then auto-merge + deploy.

Devon Price: what’s the actual deploy mechanism? i’m worried about “merged PR but router still using cached config for 30m”.

Ethan Park: consumption model: router/control plane side fetches config from control plane with ETag; TTL 60s; also push invalidation on publish. incident-bot fetches live each modal open (or caches 5m).

Allison Grant: pls ensure publish emits an audit event we can query. something like `owner_mapping_config.published` with mapping_version + diff hash.

Ethan Park: yep. audit log fields proposal:
- actor (user/service)
- source (github_pr / api)
- mapping_version
- previous_version
- change_summary (first 120 chars)
- diff_sha256
- approved_by (list)

Rafael Mendes: also need to attach incident references sometimes. like “this fix is because INC-1234”. can we add optional `reason` field?

Ethan Park: can be in PR template + commit message; but control plane can store `reason` too if we ingest PR metadata.

Mina Haddad: re schema: `secondary_owners` vs `consulted` — do we actually use consulted anywhere? or only for humans.

Dylan Brooks: incident-bot can use it to suggest additional channels to invite (e.g. `#eng-sre`, `#eng-platform-routing`). but paging should only hit primary by default.

Ravi Menon: add `escalation_policy`? e.g. after 10m no ack, page secondary? (or SRE?)

Rafael Mendes: escalation policy is separate doc (SRE incident process). for v1, keep mapping minimal. we can attach escalation rules by type in incident-bot logic, not in mapping config.

Allison Grant: +1. keep cardinality low. don’t put freeform text fields that become labels later.

Ethan Park: ok. governance:
- config repo under `platform-config/incident-owner-mapping.yaml`
- CODEOWNERS: SRE + Platform Control Plane + Routing + Infra Fleet (depending on section)
- required: 2 approvals total, one must be SRE
- emergency: 1 approval (SRE) + follow-up retro within 24h

Rafael Mendes: for “depending on section” approval logic: careful. github CODEOWNERS doesn’t do conditional ownership well.

Ethan Park: true. we can do coarse owners for file-level, or split into files per top-level type (`routing.yaml`, `capacity.yaml`, etc.).

Mina Haddad: split files. otherwise every minor routing tweak requires fleet to approve and vice versa.

Ravi Menon: +1 split. also makes diffs smaller.

Devon Price: how do we ensure mapping_version monotonic if multiple files?

Ethan Park: mapping_version can be derived from git SHA + tag. e.g. `mapping_version = git_commit_shortsha` and published_at timestamp.

Allison Grant: love commit SHA. deterministic + ties to review.

Rafael Mendes: for reporting: we just need stable `team_slug`. so mapping_version being SHA is fine.

Kira Thompson: can we require `runbook_url` for every entry? even if it’s a placeholder.

Rafael Mendes: yes, but allow `runbook_url` to be decision tree link for new subtypes until runbook exists.

Ethan Park: validation rules (fail publish if violated):
- incident_type in allowlist
- subtype in allowlist OR subtype empty for default
- exactly 1 primary_owner
- owners must be in team registry allowlist
- runbook_url must be https + confluence domain

Devon Price: also validate no duplicate keys (same type+subtype twice).

Ethan Park: yep.

Mina Haddad: rollout safety: can we canary new mapping_version to 5% of routing requests? i’d rather not.

Rafael Mendes: we don’t need canary for mapping, it’s not request path logic (mostly). but router uses it for paging? (if paging is in alerting pipeline). still: incorrect mapping is annoying but not production-breaking.

Ethan Park: router uses mapping to annotate alerts + suggest owner; it doesn’t change routing decisions. so blast radius is “wrong page / wrong channel”, not serving behavior.

Ravi Menon: ok then rollback should be instant. keep last N versions in control plane.

Ethan Park: agreed: store last 50 published versions + support pinning by version for incident forensic query.

Allison Grant: pls expose an internal endpoint: `GET /internal/owner-mapping?version=...` so dashboards/postmortems can link “mapping used”.

Rafael Mendes: and a CLI command for on-call: `rwctl owner-mapping lookup --type routing --subtype fallback_loop`.

Dylan Brooks: i can hook incident-bot to display “resolved owner from mapping_version abc1234” in the Slack modal, so it’s transparent.

Ethan Park: nice. action items:
- Ethan: draft repo layout + schema + validation (by EOW)
- Dylan/Devon: incident-bot consumption plan + UX for unknown subtype
- Rafael: confirm required audit fields + retention
- Allison: review for any observability/cardinality footguns

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: please also add a note: don’t put customer names/incident IDs in mapping entries. keep it generic.

Ethan Park: +1. will add to guidelines.

Allison Grant: final nit: team slugs need to match the canonical list. no ad-hoc like “routing-team”. use `eng-platform-routing` etc.

Ethan Park: ack. pulling from team registry service.

Kira Thompson: i’ll link the decision tree runbook url once it’s in confluence.

Rafael Mendes: thanks all. once you have a draft, drop it here and we’ll sanity check against disputed categories (routing vs fleet overload cases).
